title: Import profile (conventions)
description: How the functional documents of a group are to be read: a list of conventions, each with its evidence and who confirmed it. Open-ended on purpose: a topic or a value the engine has never seen is allowed; the well-known topics (see profile.md) only tell the reader what to look for and ask.

description.description: Who writes in this style, what the documents look like. For people picking a profile.

applies_to.description: Mapping ids read with it (a profile serves one or more mappings; scoped to the project).

derived_from.description: Profile this one started as a copy of.

layout.description: Hints on where the rules are in the document, so a second document of the group is not re-discovered from scratch. Free-form per format; the reader proposes it, the user corrects it.

columns.description: Meaning of the table columns by header text (as written) -> role (target, source, rule, mandatory, type, sample, note, version, ...).

topic.description: What the convention is about, e.g. index_base, array_notation, null_rule, mandatory_vocabulary, date_dialect, condition_scope, marker_meaning, path_separator, concatenation_operators, lookup_not_found, version_precedence. Any other string is allowed.

context.description: Where it holds when it is not everywhere: `code`, `prose`, `positional_rows`, `sheet:<name>`, `section:<title>`, ... Same topic with different contexts = different conventions.

value.description: Free: a scalar, a list, or a map (e.g. a vocabulary: {"Y": "mandatory", "N": "optional"}).

basis.description: `default` = what the reader assumes when nothing says otherwise; it is shown, never silent.

confirmed.description: true once a person agreed with it. An unconfirmed convention is applied but flagged on every rule that depends on it.

exceptions.description: Known places where the documents do not follow it.
